title: Reproduce held-neuron prediction in a two-area visual cortical dynamics model
goal: Surpass the source-paper result on the same task: Predict the held neuron’s single-trial firing-rate trajectory from the other simultaneously observed V1/LM neurons; Figure 2b residual Poisson log-likelihood is the original ordered target.
primary_outputs: Candidate method and outputs for the source task: Predict the held neuron’s single-trial firing-rate trajectory from the other simultaneously observed V1/LM neurons; Figure 2b residual Poisson log-likelihood is the original ordered target.

Source-paper comparison for Figure 2b residual Poisson log-likelihood: Residual LL = sum_t[y_t log(mu_t)-mu_t-lgamma(y_t+1)] minus the same sum for the leave-current-trial-out condition PSTH; mu is expected count per 5 ms bin. Higher is better.
success_criteria: Recover the numeric Figure 2b baseline and original trial/condition aggregation with complete seven-animal, three-fold support.
Resolve native held-target isolation, cached predictions and source-occurrence semantics before interpreting a gain.
Compare with both original constrained and unconstrained models under identical original inputs and PSTH definition.
Freeze candidate, meaningful effect, uncertainty and access/resource budgets before final evaluation.
A new trial split, training-only PSTH, reduced neuron cohort or higher line-attractor score cannot establish this paper win.
The bound improvement contract must be improvement_ready and its complete same-task comparison and admission requirements must pass.
Reproduction is calibration only; reconstructing a numerical result, changing the task or split, or achieving stronger significance alone is not success.
